messages:
rachel: quick sync: i want to propose a very small canonical handoff for hosted/dedicated/private: an "adapter ticket" (short-lived JWS) + optional install manifest. keeps routers simple.

imam: sounds good. question: is ticket admission or auth?

rachel: admission only. runtime must still verify per-request auth. ticket = proof-of-capabilities + attestation level.

tara: ops Q: air-gapped installs?

rachel: manifest-only fallback. operator uploads signed manifest; router treats it as low-attestation.

sec-bot: security checklist: tickets must include issuer, kid, tenant_hmac, capabilities_fingerprint, iat, exp. prefer mTLS binding or nonce to prevent replay.

imam: agree on replay: nonce + exp <= 60s by default. if no mTLS, force exp<=30s and anomaly scoring.

tara: feature mapping idea: local-prefix-cache -> sidecar required; streaming + generation -> ticket-only OK. we should document this matrix.

rachel: tiny example endpoints: GET /internal/v1/handshake -> runtime returns capabilities; POST /internal/v1/tickets -> runtime accepts ticket.jws.

infra-bot: created ticket INF-5001 and draft RFC rfc/adapter-ticket-2026 in docs repo.

imam: next step: short RFC with sequence diag, sample JWS, and routing precedence (attested_probe > manifest > none). schedule review Tue.

tara: +1. keeping naming short: "adapter ticket" works for me.

rachel: thanks all  i'll draft and link back here.
